reviews.text: 值得关注的游戏，看起来像是战斗，实际是小丑牌的底子，加入真实老虎机元素（和房东还是差很多），确定几个符号以后，随机roll其他符号来凑相同符号以得到尽可能多的点数，当下感觉随机因素比其他同类多了一点；精美的维京+克系外皮加大分。

《死而符生》是由iDream Interactive制作的一款老虎机×类rogue牌组构筑爬塔游戏。 本作设定在了一个被克苏鲁入侵的暗黑世界，玩家将扮演新一任的符文师，你需要携带符文之书击败马拉卡尔和他的爪牙。 整体游玩下来，尽管本作在简介中标榜了“老虎机”玩法，但实际体验与笔者的预期仍存在一定差异。其玩法核心可概括为：每回合先锁定书页上的若干符文（冥想），随后在规定的重 roll 次数内，通过反复重 roll 与锁定操作，最终确定所有符文的图案（施法）。结算时，书页上的五条法术线会从左至右，根据相同图案的连续连接长度计算倍率，进而得出最终的伤害数值。 围绕这样一套核心玩法，游戏还加入了卷轴（含禁忌卷轴）、吊坠、光环等一系列功能性道具。通过借助这些道具提升倍率、增加伤害以及改变符文图案，可搭建出风格各异的玩法流派。 本作的闯关框架与倍率设计，其实更接近《小丑牌》的风格。每闯过一关后，玩家需要根据当前自身的实力强度，选择难度不同的下一个关卡，“风险与收益相制衡”的设定和《小丑牌》“盲注”机制如出一辙；而符文宝箱开出的“增益符文”也类比于《小丑牌》改变扑克特性和筹码。 本作的难度在初期阶段还是比较低的，但随着游玩进程不断推进，难度会逐步提升：不仅 Boss 的血量会持续增加，各种减益效果也会从倍率加成、伤害输出等关键维度对玩家进行限制，进一步加大挑战难度。总的来说目前ea阶段玩法体验还是相当不错的，玩过《小丑牌》的玩家也可以光速上手。 [table][td]欢迎关注鉴赏家[url= https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44900613]“黄油收集师”[/url][/td][/table]

这是一款有着肉鸽元素的类老虎机游戏。 游戏的画面是美漫的克苏鲁风格，美术还是很不错的，看起来制作组是有美术总监的。 优化很好，游玩过程中没有卡顿，不过建议后续能加个双倍速，三倍速什么的，现在打怪符文连接画的时间还是有点长了。 游戏的背景设定是玩家所在的城镇被克苏鲁类的怪物袭击，就在这时，玩家获得了符文之书，接着就是依靠符文之书把怪物统统消灭。 玩法上还是挺有意思的，一开始各种符文书上各种符文一出来我还以为是连连看呢，结果跟着教程走了一遍，原来是个老虎机（笑）。 设定是玩家的符文书有五个竖列，每一列都有数个种类的符文，可以在流程中消除你觉得多余的符文，或者给符文增加加成。 最后横列要求就是类老虎机的算法，只要这一横能五个同种类的符文相连，以基础分乘以更高的倍率，获得数字来消灭敌人的血量。 最终要求就是在有限的施法次数下清空敌人血量。 不过算法是从左到右计算的，如果你第一个和后面四个不同，那也不会计算后面四个的倍率，而是就以第一个单独计算。 为了保证书页上的同类符文不被更换，游戏有锁定功能，这样就能通过冥想更换没被锁定的其他符文。 冥想次数有限，需要打死精英才会恢复，所以不能无脑刷新，这其实和小丑牌的设定有些类似。 可以通过卷轴，吊坠，光环等物品加成计算的倍率，还能通过卷轴和商店来清除你不需要的符文，到了后面如果能保证你的老虎机每次都能全部拉满，之后要考虑的就是如何获得更高倍率了。 目前还在EA，只有一本符文之书，后续估计会和小丑牌一样增加更多的符文之书种类，让玩家初始就能走不同的流派。 局外没有加成只有解锁，需要在局内完成特定要求之后才会解锁新的物品。 有中文。 总体来说是个玩起来很刺激的肉鸽老虎机游戏，喜欢小丑牌，幸运房东这类玩法的话就非常推荐尝试本作。 [quote]游玩百态，将游玩心得用汉语化作玩家的指明灯 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35402408/]点击这里关注汉化语录[/url] 如果喜欢这个评测，请点个赞让更多人看见[/quote]

Balatro meets slot machines, except every level has a blind. It's difficult to get the ability to shape your runes around your relics, but your relics are the only things you can guarantee access to at all times. If you haven't fought a particular enemy before, you don't know their debuff, and most of the debuffs disable certain relics. This caused me to lose the best run I've achieved because my relics were all shaped around doing lines of 5 and I ran into an enemy that disabled my 5th column. I didn't have any counterplay or adjustments to make, I just hit an enemy effect that shut off my ability to function and lost. Not recommended because the extra layer of RNG on enemy effects isn't fun or interesting, it just randomly kills runs that were otherwise going super well.

《死而符生》是由iDream Interactive制作的一款类小丑牌的肉鸽爬塔游戏，不过游戏形式是以一种类老虎机的方式呈现的。游戏既有玩家可以提升对应构筑的道具和饰品，又有随机投掷符文的惊喜感，只要成功构筑一类符文就可以感受到秒杀BOSS清空血条的爽快感，当然也需要玩家一定的策略，不然很容易在第二大关的时候被增长的敌方血量追平优势，卡关于此。 [h2]游戏玩法 [/h2] 局内游戏的桌面上一共有三行五列符文，有八种颜色，分别属于八种元素，同样的元素可以以横、斜的方式进行伤害累计。玩家有两个数值，底部左边蓝色的相当于重置次数，使用过的次数需要打败三轮敌人才能恢复，玩家最多可以锁定8个符文，其他的符文会进行重置；右边红色的施法相当于玩家的攻击次数，每次施法都要从左侧第一列开始依次往右计算，玩家必须在次数用光之前清空敌人的血量，否则就会被视为失败。 游戏左侧是饰品栏位，可以从根本上提高或者改变玩家的游戏体验，比如有的能把玩家达成的连起来的符文数加一；有的则会从更基础的伤害和倍率上提高；有的甚至会指定第几列的符文有什么效果。而且符文的先后顺序也会影响伤害的计算，有些是在最后一击才能生效的饰品，有些则是每一击都会生效。调整好顺序伤害也会成倍的增长。此外饰品上面还可以在商店进行宝石的镶嵌，会附加一些额外buff，个人比较常用的就是蓝宝石，可以增加一次施法机会。 [h2]符文构筑 [/h2] 和很多类小丑牌游戏一样，本作也提供更高级品质的符文石，附带一些特定的buff，可以放在任意一个牌组里，但这个于升级还是不一样的，原本的低级符文石还在，需要在特定的关卡之后铁匠铺砸碎符文的环节减少其他类别或者低级符文的持有。一旦能构筑好一套牌组，至少前两次施法我们可以获得最大的伤害点数。 [h2]卷轴系统 [/h2] 这个就相当于其他游戏里的道具，是消耗品，功能也是五花八门，有些会直接作用在符文石上，比如消除后加1金币、增加一定概率的倍率加成。有些则是会作用在饰品和金币上，个人最喜欢刷钱的那个道具，运气好直接翻一倍，差一点增加个三分之一也不是难事。 [h2]总结 [/h2] 《死而符生》是一款比较有难度的类小丑牌游戏，需要玩家专心经营一两个流派，中途更改的概率很低，不过一旦成型还是非常爽快的。美术风格也不差，有点克苏鲁的感觉，敌人的种类也蛮多的，期待后续更新能加入更多的敌人和构筑流派，玩过小丑牌等类似游戏的玩家可以尝试一下。 [quote]漫话漫谈，期待关注:[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44551694/]写生漫话家[/url] ←节约宝贵时间，阅读省流测评~ 欢迎加入漫话家的大家庭:[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/14030826]写生漫话家[/url]←共同探讨游戏中的精彩片段，向玩家展现第九艺术的魅力~

I’m typically pretty good at these types of games, beat all of stp, balatro, etc… This game has almost 0 strategy or build balance. Everything depends on trinkets though or removing runes, the one time you get a good build a boss will likely exact counter it, whether that be wilds or amuletting your runes, which if you don’t roll a good rng for the npc that destroys runes (and it’s exponentially expensive to remove the amulets). Pretty much like no strategy in this, it’s all rng and there is zero forgiveness, add in the slow animations even when maxed out at 8x, you spend like 30 minutes before meeting the one boss that will destroy your build. Have to hold an entire column? Legit a death sentence. I don’t leave negative reviews often but I tried the game for a decently long time with multiple strategies and the furthest I have gotten is like end of chapter 4 or so… Sucks cause it would be a fun game, but the rng just ruins it; even in megabonk it lets you turn off some items/weapons to make some builds viable. Just my opinion, but not worth the time you will put into it.

Balatro slot game. Okay concept IMO, but unless you manage to snowball with a viable combination of trinkets in the early game, it's really hard to get your gold up to buy scrolls with which to remove symbols and mitigate the RNG factor, which is why I believe some reviewers are complaining that it's too random. Still recommend it though. Update 21/04: I have refunded the game as it's not very fun. It has lifted a lot of its systems from Balatro and tried to apply them to slots which just doesn't work very well. The randomness and bad RNG is fine and expected from a roguelike, but the developer should look closer at how CloverPit stole from Balatro and consider taking a page from their book. Also, maybe consider adding active item and/or ability mechanics, as the gameplay overall feels very sterile to me.

"Balatro" but with magic elemental slot machine. Surprisingly fresh. I respect it when games that wear their inspiration on their sleeves, and boy does this game ever. If you've played and enjoyed Balatro you are already most of the way to enjoying this game. You have a 5 column slot machine that has a balanced inventory of 7 elemental color runes. There are 5 different lines to match runes on with a single pull of the slot machine. With that established... Balatro Migration guide: - each triggered line has a base damage (blue) number and a base multiplier (red) number. they get multiplied to do damage. - instead of 4 suits and 13 numbers, you have elements (which are both the base damage and matching component. - instead of jokers you have trinkets - instead of card packs you have scrolls - instead of seals you have amulets - instead of editions you have auras As with Balatro you pick your poison along the way, choosing challenges and rewards. Your task is to continually invest in making a more consistent and broken scoring engine. It inherits a lot of pros/cons of Balatro Actual pros of this game as its own thing: - surprisingly good aesthetics; the same concept could have been done much uglier. - having the runes in an elemental loop makes it more fun to convert them up and down as you go for homogenous rune pools. - meta progression is well tuned and encourages you to play a variety of starting loadouts and strategies. Cons: - the joy in a slot machine is generally the randomness as you do several pulls hoping for a jackpot. In this game your best strategy is to remove almost all that joy by engineering a slot machine that reliably gives a jackpot. There's more nuance to it than this for sure, but like Balatro it's got a base game that you optimize the fun out of. And from there you need to try and optimize it even further. - more line variety could be fun idk. So far it's a handful of books with the same line patterns and 4 books with unique line patterns. Overall it has much more in common with Balatro than it does with other roguelite slot games, and there's room for everybody. It does things differently than Luck be a Landlord or Slots and Daggers.

Runeborn is a dark fantasy roguelike developed by iDream Interactive and published by Goblinz Publishing and Astrolabe Games that successfully combines deckbuilding concepts with an innovative rune-spinning combat system. In a genre filled with card battlers and traditional roguelikes, the game distinguishes itself through a combat mechanic that feels fresh while still retaining the strategic depth that fans of the genre expect. Instead of simply building a deck and playing cards, players construct a magical Runebook and manipulate spinning rune combinations to unleash powerful abilities against increasingly dangerous enemies. Set in a grim world threatened by the forces of Malakar, the game places players in the role of a powerful Runeborn warrior tasked with pushing back the darkness. While the narrative remains secondary to the gameplay, the setting provides a compelling backdrop for the adventure. Ancient magic, cursed creatures, mystical artifacts, and hostile landscapes create an atmosphere that supports the game's dark fantasy identity. The story serves primarily as a framework for progression, allowing players to focus on experimentation, combat, and character growth. The most distinctive feature is unquestionably the combat system. Rather than drawing cards directly into a hand, players spin rune columns that generate various magical combinations. Matching symbols across multiple lines activates spells, attacks, defensive abilities, and special effects. Initially, the mechanic resembles a slot machine, but beneath that surface lies a surprisingly strategic system. Success depends less on luck and more on preparation, rune selection, and understanding how different combinations interact with one another. A particularly clever aspect of the design is the ability to lock runes into place. This mechanic gives players meaningful control over future outcomes and transforms combat into a careful balancing act between risk and reward. Deciding which symbols to preserve and which reels to reroll creates constant tension during battles. Every turn presents new possibilities, forcing players to adapt while still pursuing long-term strategies. This balance between unpredictability and player agency is one of the game's greatest achievements. Customization is at the heart of the experience. Throughout each run, players continuously modify their Runebook by adding new runes, removing weaker options, and refining their strategy. Every decision directly impacts future encounters, encouraging experimentation with different approaches. Some builds focus on overwhelming damage output, while others prioritize status effects, defensive tactics, or complex chain reactions. The flexibility of the system ensures that players can develop unique strategies rather than following a single optimal path. The trinket system adds another impressive layer of depth. Powerful magical items collected during a run can dramatically alter how a build functions. Some trinkets enhance specific rune types, while others multiply damage, trigger bonus effects, or completely change combat priorities. Discovering powerful synergies between trinkets and runes often becomes the key to success. Few moments are more satisfying than finding an unexpected combination that transforms an average run into an unstoppable force. Replayability is one of Runeborn's strongest qualities. Randomized encounters, changing rewards, evolving builds, and a large variety of rune combinations ensure that no two journeys feel identical. Even failed attempts contribute to the learning process, encouraging players to rethink strategies and explore new possibilities. This constant cycle of experimentation and discovery creates the addictive gameplay loop that defines the best roguelikes. Enemy encounters remain engaging because opponents possess unique abilities that require different tactical responses. Some enemies focus on direct aggression, while others rely on debuffs, defensive mechanics, or disruptive abilities. Elite encounters and boss battles provide even greater challenges, forcing players to fully utilize the strengths of their builds. These tougher fights often become the highlights of a run because they test both preparation and adaptability. The progression system rewards calculated decision-making. As players advance through the game, they earn currency that can be spent in specialized shops. These merchants offer opportunities to strengthen builds through new runes, upgrades, and rare trinkets. Resource management becomes an important strategic consideration, as spending too aggressively can leave players vulnerable later while excessive saving may result in missed opportunities. Visually, Runeborn embraces a stylish dark fantasy aesthetic filled with magical effects, ominous environments, and distinctive enemy designs. The user interface is well organized despite the complexity of the systems beneath it. Information is presented clearly, making it easier to understand active effects, rune combinations, and combat outcomes. The visual feedback accompanying successful spell activations is especially satisfying, helping reinforce the impact of powerful plays. The sound design complements the atmosphere effectively. Magical attacks feel impactful, enemies produce memorable audio cues, and the soundtrack reinforces the game's dark fantasy tone. While the audio may not be revolutionary, it succeeds in enhancing immersion and maintaining the mood throughout extended play sessions. One area where some players may struggle is the initial learning curve. The interactions between runes, trinkets, and various effects can feel overwhelming during the first few runs. Understanding how to maximize synergy requires experimentation and patience. However, this complexity ultimately becomes one of the game's strengths because it creates a rewarding sense of mastery as players become more familiar with the systems. Balance is generally strong, though certain combinations can occasionally feel significantly more powerful than others. Some builds naturally develop more easily than alternatives, which may lead players toward familiar strategies after many hours. Nevertheless, the sheer number of possible combinations ensures that there is always room for creative experimentation. What ultimately makes Runeborn stand out is its willingness to innovate within a genre that often relies on familiar formulas. By combining deckbuilding principles with a rune-based spinning system, it creates a combat experience that feels distinct from both traditional card games and standard roguelikes. Every run offers opportunities for discovery, adaptation, and unexpected success, making progression consistently engaging. Runeborn is an imaginative and highly replayable roguelike that succeeds through its original mechanics, deep customization options, and rewarding strategic gameplay. Its blend of rune manipulation, build crafting, trinket synergy, and dark fantasy atmosphere creates an experience that feels both familiar and refreshingly new. While the complexity may require some patience from newcomers, players willing to learn its systems will find a deeply satisfying adventure filled with endless experimentation and meaningful decision-making.
